faqs.a:
(a)
Generally.
The city shall have the right of entry to survey any structure or premises within
               the city for the presence of a cross-connection, to inspect a cross-connection, to
               assess possible contamination risk, to test the backflow assembly or method, to audit
               any backflow assembly or method, to determine compliance with this article, whenever
               there is reasonable cause to believe there exists in a structure or upon a premises
               a condition in violation of this article, or otherwise to enforce this Code. This
               right of entry shall be a condition of water service in order to protect the health,
               safety and welfare of customers throughout the city's distribution system.
(b)
Process.
The director is authorized to exercise the city's right of entry at reasonable times
               to perform the duties imposed by this Code. If the structure or premises is occupied,
               the director shall present credentials to the occupant and request entry. If the structure
               or premises is unoccupied, the director shall first make a reasonable effort to contact
               the owner or other person having charge or control of the structure or premises and
               request entry. If entry is refused, the director may apply to the municipal court
               for a warrant if the warrant relates to a violation of this article, involves a serious
               threat to public safety or order, and the violation is not also a violation prohibited
               by state statute for which a search warrant could be issued by a district or county
               court. The purpose of the warrant may be to enter the premises and any structure thereon
               to survey the premises and any structure thereon for the presence of a cross-connection,
               to search for and inspect the uncontrolled connection or source of the suspected contamination
               risk, to collect water samples, to assess possible contamination risk, to audit or
               test the backflow assembly or method, and to determine compliance with and otherwise
               enforce this article. The director shall also have recourse to any other remedy provided
               by law to secure entry.
(
Ord. No. 4829
, § 1, 12-5-2022)
